youtube_title: Lake Michigan, 1937: the captain who vanished from his own ship
body: On the night of April 28, 1937, Captain George Doner was bringing the freighter O.S. McFarland from Erie, Pennsylvania, to Port Washington, Wisconsin. Later accounts say he went to his cabin to rest and asked to be called when the ship neared port, and that when a crewman went to wake him, he was not there. No sign of him was ever found. Some versions say the cabin door was locked from the inside; the 1937 Associated Press report doesn't mention that. One account of the 1937 coverage says his crew believed he fell overboard. Today it's told as part of the 'Lake Michigan Triangle'. (Many retellings spell his name Donner and call the ship the O.M. McFarland; the 1937 report says Doner and O.S. McFarland.)
